stem: Phosphorus, sulfur and chlorine can all react with oxygen to form oxides.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: Phosphorus reacts with an excess of oxygen to form phosphorus(V) oxide.
parts.text: Write an equation to show the reaction of phosphorus with excess oxygen.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Describe the reaction of phosphorus(V) oxide with water.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: State the structure and bonding of solid phosphorus(V) oxide.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
The two most common oxides of sulfur are $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{SO}_3$.

When $\text{SO}_2$ dissolves in water, a small proportion of it reacts with water to form a weak Brønsted-Lowry acid.
parts.text: Explain the meaning of the term weak Brønsted-Lowry acid.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction of $\text{SO}_2$ with water.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
$\text{SO}_2$ reacts with $\text{NO}_2$ in the atmosphere to form $\text{SO}_3$ and $\text{NO}$.

NO is then oxidised in air to form $\text{NO}_2$.

$$\text{SO}_2 + \text{NO}_2 \rightarrow \text{SO}_3 + \text{NO}$$

$$2\text{NO} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2$$

State the role of $\text{NO}_2$ in this two-stage process.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
Emissions of $\text{SO}_2$ from coal-fired power stations can be reduced by mixing the coal with powdered limestone.

Limestone is heated to form $\text{CaO}$ in reaction 1. This then reacts with $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ to form $\text{CaSO}_4$ in reaction 2.

reaction 1:

$$\text{CaCO}_3\text{(s)} \rightarrow \text{CaO}\text{(s)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$$

reaction 2:

$$\text{CaO}\text{(s)} + \text{SO}_2\text{(g)} + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CaSO}_4\text{(s)}$$
parts.text: State the type of reaction occurring in reaction 1.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Use the data to calculate the enthalpy change of reaction 2.

| compound | $\Delta H_{\text{f}}/\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{CaO}\text{(s)}$ | $-635$ |
| $\text{SO}_2\text{(g)}$ | $-297$ |
| $\text{CaSO}_4\text{(s)}$ | $-1434$ |

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem: Chlorine forms several oxides, including $\text{Cl}_2\text{O}$, $\text{ClO}_2$ and $\text{Cl}_2\text{O}_6$.
parts.text: Draw a 'dot-and-cross' diagram of $\text{Cl}_2\text{O}$. Show outer-shell electrons only.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
(d)(iii)
parts.text:
$\text{Cl}_2\text{O}_6\text{(g)}$ is produced by the reaction of $\text{ClO}_2\text{(g)}$ with $\text{O}_3\text{(g)}$.

$$2\text{ClO}_2\text{(g)} + 2\text{O}_3\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{Cl}_2\text{O}_6\text{(g)} + 2\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \quad \Delta H = -216\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

The reaction takes place at $500\text{ K}$ and $100\text{ kPa}$.

State and explain the effect on the yield of $\text{Cl}_2\text{O}_6\text{(g)}$ when the experiment is carried out:

- at $1000\text{ K}$ and $100\text{ kPa}$

- at $500\text{ K}$ and $500\text{ kPa}$.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem:
Element **E** is a Period 5 element.

**E** reacts with oxygen to form an insoluble white oxide that has a melting point of $1910^{\circ}\text{C}$. The oxide of **E** conducts electricity only when liquid.

**E** also reacts readily with $\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$ to form a white solid that reacts exothermically with water. The resulting solution reacts with aqueous silver nitrate to form a white precipitate that dissolves in dilute ammonia.
parts.text: Suggest the type of bonding shown by the **oxide** of **E**. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest the type of bonding shown by the **chloride** of **E**. Explain your answer.
